mechanism_narrative: The current level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is inversely related to S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, with lower rates reducing the discount rate for equity valuation and increasing expected returns.
failure_condition: The correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is not negative and statistically significant (p>=0.05) over the last 5 years, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5%, it signals a tightening monetary policy that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, the 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 5.0% and employment (PAYEMS) falls below 134000 thousand persons, it signals a deteriorating labor market that reduces consumer spending and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods meeting the trigger condition (UNRATE>5.0% AND PAYEMS<134000), the 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle defined by FEDFUNDS exceeding 4.5% and CPIAUCSL exceeding 2.5%, the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to rising inflation expectations and policy tightening.
failure_condition: In periods meeting the trigger condition (FEDFUNDS>4.5% AND CPIAUCSL>2.5%), the 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The current level of industrial production (INDPRO) is positively related to S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as higher industrial output signals robust economic activity that supports equity valuations.
failure_condition: The correlation between INDPRO and 20-day returns is not positive and statistically significant (p>=0.05) over the last 5 years, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 2000 thousand units, it signals a weakening real estate market that reduces consumer confidence and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods when HOUST < 2000, the 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When residential sales (RSAFS) exceed 350500 million dollars and GDP (GDPC1) falls below 11050 billion dollars, it signals a disconnect between strong housing demand and weak overall economic growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods meeting the trigger condition (RSAFS>350500 AND GDPC1<11050), the 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The current level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is inversely related to S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, with lower rates reducing the discount rate for equity valuation and increasing expected returns due to immediate market reactions.
failure_condition: The correlation between FEDFUNDS and 5-day returns is not negative and statistically significant (p>=0.05) over the last 5 years, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
